Story time. That's what this 'verse is for, right?

So, picture me about 1.5 years ago. Five-foot-nine white boy from Texas who is big into theatre. It's late January in my junior year of high school, and I'd managed to get a part in the winter play: Cash On Delivery, a hilarious British farce by Michael Cooney. It is the day before we open the show. Said show itself is about Eric, a guy who has been defrauding the Department of Social Services by claiming every type of benefit possible for the innumerable people he claims are living at his house. He decides to get out of the game by killing these fake people one by one... just a little bit too late. A DSS inspector shows up one day, and things go downhill from there. Eric recruits Norman (one of his actual tenants; I played him) and George (Eric's uncle) into the mix to try to outwit everyone. It's gut-busting, especially when the inspector gets drunk and fights Eric's washing machine with a plunger.

Anyhow, throughout the course of the show, I go from being all giddy about getting married next week, to discovering that Eric used my name in his scheme, to pretending to be my own son (who is a deaf piano tuner; don't ask), and then simultaneously convincing the inspector that I am Eric's wife, and convincing my fiancee that I am not dead. For that second-to-last one, I had to put on a dress, heels, corset, and wig. Going into full-on "fuck it" mode, I decided to put on drag makeup as well. The disguise works for a moment, until Eric's actual wife is on stage at the same time as me, and the jig is up.

There was the wig. Oh my god, the wig. It was a very long, blonde P.O.S. with a ton of split ends; with each costumed rehearsal it got more and more tangled. During the last day of tech week, it was little more than an awkward golden plastic-y ball of itchiness. The director had us lowly cast members violently take the wig off of me and put it back on as necessary. Towards the end of the show, I'm supposed to jam the wig on my head and dart across the stage before the inspector's supervisor sees me. Which I do just fine, but Eric's wife enters just to rip the wig back off. During that rehearsal, I'd stumbled a bit during my darting and fixed the wig when I stopped. I must've gotten a couple bundles of hair wrapped around my neck or something, because when the girl playing Eric's wife went to rip the wig off... she kinda didn't. One yank, no movement. Two yanks, something doesn't feel right. Three yanks, four, I manage to gag but then nothing. Things were getting a bit hazy, and by the fifth or sixth yank (I lost count) I'd fallen over and the rehearsal was stopped.

After a few minutes of "holy fuck, I was almost killed" and "the last thing my friends would see me wearing would've been a fucking dress" I casually asked if we could stop rehearsing for the night. When the director asked if I was alright I shouted "NO!" and walked to the dressing room to get the makeup off of me.
Cross-dressing for the Stage, or That One Time When I was Almost Strangled by a Wig
Aside from that, it's still my favorite show I've been in. Next ones were a gangster in The Drowsy Chaperone and Theseus in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
